title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Low-Resource Medical Triage Chatbots
note: Demonstrates chaining: the 9-section, ~2000-word paper is split into 3 chunks by chunk_paper(), tagged and extracted independently, then merged by P3 into one coherent summary.

checked_summary.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Low-Resource Medical Triage Chatbots
checked_summary.problem: Medical triage chatbots are well studied in English but not in low-resource languages, where labeled triage dialogue data is scarce, creating a gap for regions where healthcare access is lowest and the local languages are least represented in NLP research.
checked_summary.method: The paper transfers an English-trained triage dialogue policy (a multilingual sentence encoder plus a small trainable policy head) to five low-resource languages using only 200 in-language dialogues per language for fine-tuning, and tests an additional back-translation augmentation step on top of that fine-tuning.
checked_summary.results: Zero-shot transfer reaches 58% average routing accuracy across the five languages; fine-tuning on 200 in-language dialogues raises this to 74% (81% of the English ceiling of 91%); adding back-translation augmentation raises it further to 79%. Khmer is the hardest language under every condition.
checked_summary.limitations: The study covers only five low-resource languages and one clinical partner's triage schema, and back-translation quality for Khmer and Quechua is weaker than for Tagalog and Swahili, which likely explains part of the remaining accuracy gap. The system was evaluated offline against expert-labeled dialogues only, not with live patients.
